      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or SHA1 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or MD5 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or SHA1 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or MD5 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shai-Hulud npm preinstall: node spawns Bun runtime from bun-dl-* tmpdir AIInstallation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's signature execution chain where the malicious npm preinstall hook (node setup.mjs) downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime to a mkdtempSync-created directory prefixed bun-dl- and then executes execution.js under Bun to evade EDRs that only watch for node children of npm install. Targets the exact loader behaviour in setup.mjs (SHA256 4066781f...) shared across mbt@1.2.48 and the three compromised @cap-js packages. Rationale: Pivots on the exact mkdtempSync prefix 'bun-dl-' and the platform-specific Bun release-asset names (bun-windows-x64-baseline, bun-linux-x64-baseline, bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline, bun-linux-aarch64, bun-darwin) hard-coded in setup.mjs (SHA256 4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34), plus the literal 'execution.js' filename — the article calls out 'a different binary name that bypasses' EDR monitors of node children, which is the exact behaviour this UC flips back into a detection. IOCs taken directly from StepSecurity's runtime trace.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where (FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
      or FolderPath has "bun-dl-"
      or FolderPath has "bun-windows-x64-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-x64-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-aarch64"
      or FolderPath has "bun-darwin"
      or ProcessCommandLine has "execution.js")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","preinstall","npm install","yarn install","pnpm install")
   or FolderPath has "bun-dl-"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun-dl-","bun-windows-x64-baseline","bun-linux-x64-baseline","bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline","bun-linux-aarch64","bun-darwin","execution.js")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","preinstall","npm install","yarn install","pnpm install")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has "bun-dl-"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shai-Hulud AI coding-agent persistence: .claude/settings.json + .vscode/tasks.json drops AIInstallation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's novel persistence mechanism where the payload commits or writes .claude/settings.json (abusing Claude Code's SessionStart hook) and .vscode/tasks.json (with runOn:folderOpen) into every accessible repository. Any developer re-opening the repo in VSCode or Claude Code silently re-executes the malware — this is one of the first supply-chain campaigns weaponising AI-agent config files. Rationale: The article describes 'one of the first supply chain attacks to target AI coding agent configurations as a persistence and propagation vector', specifically dropping .claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook abuse) and .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen. Detection bucket-aggregates both filenames in a 1h window because the loader writes them as a pair, and falls back to the suspect-parent process list (node/bun/git) when only one of the two files is observed — that combination is essentially nil in legitimate developer activity. Sigma omitted because the detection is a multi-file correlation, not a single event.
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let _window = 1h;
let _suspect_files = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where (FolderPath endswith @"\.claude\settings.json"
          or FolderPath endswith "/.claude/settings.json"
          or FolderPath endswith @"\.vscode\tasks.json"
          or FolderPath endswith "/.vscode/tasks.json")
    | extend FileKind = case(
        FolderPath has ".claude", "claude_settings",
        FolderPath has ".vscode", "vscode_tasks",
        "other")
    | extend Bucket = bin(Timestamp, _window);
_suspect_files
| summarize FilesDropped = make_set(FileKind),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Paths = make_set(FolderPath, 50),
            Initiators = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 20),
            InitiatingCmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 20)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Bucket
| where array_length(FilesDropped) >= 2
   or Initiators has_any ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","git.exe","git")
| order by FirstSeen desc
let _window = 1h;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath endswith @"\.claude\settings.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith "/.claude/settings.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith @"\.vscode\tasks.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith "/.vscode/tasks.json")
| extend FileKind = case(
    TargetFilePath has ".claude", "claude_settings",
    TargetFilePath has ".vscode", "vscode_tasks",
    "other")
| extend Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, _window)
| summarize FilesDropped = make_set(FileKind),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50),
            Actors = make_set(ActorUsername, 20),
            ActingProcs = make_set(ActingProcessName, 20),
            ActingCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 20)
            by DvcHostname, Bucket
| where array_length(FilesDropped) >= 2
   or ActingProcs has_any ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","git.exe","git")
| order by FirstSeen desc

Shai-Hulud known-bad setup.mjs / execution.js SHA256 hash match AIInstallation High
Detects on-disk or in-execution presence of the two Shai-Hulud loader/payload files by their byte-identical SHA256 hashes — the setup.mjs loader (4066781f...) is identical across all four confirmed compromised packages (mbt@1.2.48, @cap-js/sqlite@2.2.2, @cap-js/postgres@v2.2.2, @cap-js/db-service@v2.10.1), and execution.js (80a3d287...) is the 11.6 MB obfuscated credential stealer. This is the highest-fidelity retrospective hunt across npm-using hosts and CI runners. Rationale: The article explicitly states setup.mjs is 'SHA-256 (identical across all compromised packages) 4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34' and execution.js for mbt@1.2.48 is 80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac. These are the highest-fidelity IOCs in the campaign — byte-identical across four packages confirms the same operator/toolchain. Union across file, process and image-load tables ensures retrospective coverage whether the artifact landed on disk only, was executed, or was loaded.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let _ShaiHulud_Hashes = dynamic([
    "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",  // setup.mjs (loader, identical across all 4 compromised packages)
    "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"   // execution.js (11.6MB obfuscated payload from mbt@1.2.48)
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ProcessCreated", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, Source="DeviceProcessEvents" ),
    ( DeviceImageLoadEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ImageLoaded", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine="",
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc
let _ShaiHulud_Hashes = dynamic([
    "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",
    "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes) or Hash in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,
                  Hash = coalesce(TargetFileSHA256, Hash), ActingProcessName, ActorUsername,
                  Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType="ProcessCreated",
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  Hash = SHA256, ActingProcessName = ParentProcessName,
                  ActorUsername, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

elementary-data Compromised on PyPI and GHCR: Forged Release Pushed via GitHub Actions Script Injection

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Install of trojaned elementary-data 0.23.3 via pip / poetry / uv · [LLM] Docker / Kubernetes pull of compromised ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary image
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious elementary.pth dropped in Python site-packages · Article-specific behavioural hunt — elementary-data Compromised on PyPI and GHCR: Forged Release Pushed via GitHub A
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound to elementary-data exfil C2 igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.sky · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Stage-3 exfil archive trin.tar.gz POST via curl --data-binary · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Outbound to elementary-data exfil C2 igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.sky AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS resolution, HTTP/S egress, or proxy traffic to the credential-stealer C2 hard-coded in the trojaned elementary-data 0.23.3 .pth payload. A single hit anywhere in the org indicates a host has installed the compromised PyPI package or pulled the trojaned ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary image and that the stage-3 collector has reached the network. Rationale: Anchored on the single hard-coded exfil host igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud named in the StepSecurity write-up. Any DNS / HTTP egress to this host is unambiguous: the domain has no benign use case and was registered for this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205 • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal SOC sandbox detonations of the trojaned package (whitelist sandbox source IPs)
  • Security researchers manually resolving the IOC during triage from analyst workstations
  • Threat-intel platform IOC enrichment workers (e.g. VirusTotal / OPSWAT relays in your tenant)
  • DNS sinkhole/SIE feeds replaying historical queries
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox", "detonation", "sec-research")) and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("vt-uploader.exe", "opswat-relay.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm which process on the source host issued the lookup — pivot to DeviceProcessEvents for python.exe / docker-shim / kubelet ancestry, and check whether `elementary.pth` exists under any site-packages. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the C2 domain at the egress proxy / DNS RPZ, and rotate every credential the host could touch — AWS access keys, GCP ADC, Azure tokens, kubeconfigs, gh tokens, SSH keys, npm/pypi/cargo tokens, and crypto wallets — assume harvested. 3) Hunt: inventory all hosts and CI runners that ran `pip install elementary-data==0.23.3` or pulled `ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary:{0.23.3,latest}`; query the registry/proxy logs for prior pulls of digest sha256:31ecc5939de6...634255.
let MaliciousDomain = "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud";
let WindowDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceNetworkEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
        | where RemoteUrl has MaliciousDomain
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source = "DeviceNetworkEvents"),
    (DeviceEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
        | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
        | where AdditionalFields has MaliciousDomain or RemoteUrl has MaliciousDomain
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort = toint(0), Source = "DeviceEvents(DNS)")
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousDomain = "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud";
let WindowDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where DnsQuery has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, SrcHost = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, Indicator = DnsQuery, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where Name has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = Computer, SrcIP = ClientIP, Indicator = Name, Source = "DnsEvents"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where DestinationHostName has MaliciousDomain or RequestURL has MaliciousDomain or DestinationDnsDomain has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = SourceHostName, SrcIP = SourceIP, Indicator = coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), Source = "CommonSecurityLog"),
    (Syslog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where SyslogMessage has MaliciousDomain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcHost = HostName, SrcIP = HostIP, Indicator = SyslogMessage, Source = "Syslog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious elementary.pth dropped in Python site-packages AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the trojaned `elementary.pth` loader inside any Python site-packages directory. Legitimate elementary-data releases ship no top-level .pth file; this file is unique to 0.23.3 and is what triggers payload execution on every Python interpreter startup. Rationale: The article confirms `elementary.pth` is the single malicious artifact added in 0.23.3 vs 0.23.2 and that no legitimate elementary release ships a .pth file — making the filename in site-packages a near-zero-FP signal. Size gate of 50KB further separates the ~245KB base64 payload from any legit user-created .pth. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205 • https://pypi.org/project/elementary-data/
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandbox detonation of the IOC for analysis (filter by host tag)
  • Forensic acquisition tooling copying the file into evidence folders (not really FP — investigate the source host)
  • Backup/restore of a previously-infected snapshot (still need to remediate)
  • Developer manually reproducing the issue in a venv for triage
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox", "detonation")) and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("forensics-collector.exe", "velociraptor.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm file SHA256 and size; collect the file; check the parent process — `pip.exe` / `pip3` / `python -m pip` indicates install via PyPI, while `dockerd` / `containerd` indicates a container layer extract. 2) Contain: isolate the host or kill the container, delete the .pth file, kill any python.exe processes that may have already loaded the payload. 3) Hunt: pull `pip install` history and lockfiles across the org for `elementary-data==0.23.3`; check Argo CD / k8s manifests for `ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary:latest` or `:0.23.3`; rotate any credentials reachable by the infected host (see UC #1 runbook).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "elementary.pth"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\site-packages\\", "/site-packages/", "/dist-packages/")
| extend IsOversized = (FileSize > 50000)  // legit .pth files are <1KB; payload is ~245KB
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, IsOversized,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "elementary.pth"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\site-packages\\", "/site-packages/", "/dist-packages/")
| extend IsOversized = (TargetFileSize > 50000)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, IsOversized, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Install of trojaned elementary-data 0.23.3 via pip / poetry / uv AIDelivery High
Detects any package manager invocation requesting the malicious pinned version `elementary-data==0.23.3` (or the unpinned `latest`/`>=0.23.3` form that PyPI still resolves to the trojaned release at the time of the StepSecurity report). Catches the install moment so the host can be quarantined before the .pth fires on next interpreter startup. Rationale: Article names the exact poisoned version (0.23.3) and the package canonical names (`elementary-data` / `elementary_data`). Process-create with these two strings in the command line is high-fidelity because no benign install would target a known-malicious pinned version after the StepSecurity disclosure. Cross-checked against: • https://pypi.org/project/elementary-data/#history • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Detection engineer reproducing the install in an isolated VM
  • Sandbox / CI pipeline that intentionally installs the IOC to validate this very detection
  • Forensic re-installation of the package to confirm scope on a known-infected host
  • Backup restore of an old lockfile that referenced 0.23.3 before the .pth payload existed (rare — 0.23.3 was always malicious)
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox", "ci-detonation", "sec-lab")) and not (AccountName in~ ("detection-eng", "redteam"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the install actually succeeded (look for the follow-up `elementary.pth` write — see UC #2) and whether the python interpreter that consumes the venv has been launched yet. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill running python processes that loaded the venv, `pip uninstall elementary-data` then re-install 0.23.4 (the clean replacement noted in issue #2205). 3) Hunt: scan code repos, Dockerfiles, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Pipfile.lock, conda env.yml across the org for `elementary-data==0.23.3` or any unpinned `elementary-data` reference; check CI artefacts produced during the window 2026-04-24T22:20Z → 2026-04-25 for cached wheels.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip.exe", "pip3.exe", "pip", "pip3", "poetry.exe", "poetry", "uv.exe", "uv", "python.exe", "python3", "python")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe", "pip3.exe", "poetry.exe", "uv.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("==0.23.3", " 0.23.3", "elementary_data-0.23.3", "elementary-data-0.23.3")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("install", "add", "sync") and not(ProcessCommandLine has "==0.23.4" or ProcessCommandLine has "<0.23.3"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\pip.exe", "\\pip3.exe", "\\poetry.exe", "\\uv.exe", "\\python.exe")
        | where CommandLine has "elementary-data"
        | where CommandLine has_any ("==0.23.3", " 0.23.3", "elementary_data-0.23.3", "elementary-data-0.23.3")
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName),
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetProcessName has_any ("pip", "pip3", "poetry", "uv", "python")
        | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data"
        | where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "0.23.3") or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "0.23.3")
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Install of Compromised elementary-data 0.23.3 PyPI Package
id: 4d9a8c63-2e7b-4f5a-8c1d-9e0f1a2b3c84
description: Detects pip / poetry / uv invocation installing the trojaned elementary-data 0.23.3 release.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\pip.exe'
      - '\pip3.exe'
      - '\poetry.exe'
      - '\uv.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
      - '/poetry'
      - '/uv'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'elementary-data'
      - '0.23.3'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_cmd
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) AND (@Image:(*\\pip.exe OR *\\pip3.exe OR *\\poetry.exe OR *\\uv.exe OR *\\python.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/pip OR */pip3 OR */poetry OR */uv OR */python OR */python3)) AND @CommandLine:(*elementary-data*0.23.3* OR *elementary_data-0.23.3*) OR @process.command_line:(*elementary-data*0.23.3* OR *elementary_data-0.23.3*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(pip|pip3|poetry|uv|python|python3)(\.exe)?$/i CommandLine=/elementary[-_]data/i CommandLine=/0\.23\.3/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","poetry","poetry.exe","uv","uv.exe","python.exe","python3","python")) AND (Processes.process="*elementary-data==0.23.3*" OR Processes.process="*elementary-data 0.23.3*" OR Processes.process="*elementary_data-0.23.3*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","poetry","poetry.exe","uv","uv.exe","python.exe","python3","python")) AND (Processes.process="*elementary-data==0.23.3*" OR Processes.process="*elementary-data 0.23.3*" OR Processes.process="*elementary_data-0.23.3*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Docker / Kubernetes pull of compromised ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary image AIDelivery High
Detects docker, containerd, podman, crictl, kubectl, or kubelet pulls of the trojaned GHCR image — including the dangerous unpinned `:latest` form that resolved to the malicious digest sha256:31ecc5939de6...634255 between 2026-04-24 and the cleanup. Fires on the pull itself rather than at runtime so deployments can be blocked before the container ever runs the .pth payload. Rationale: Anchored on the exact registry path called out in the article (`ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary`) and the known-bad digest prefix (`sha256:31ecc5939de6...634255`). Catches both Docker CLI users and Kubernetes admission for image creates — the article specifically warns that `:latest` resolved to the trojaned image for every team that didn't pin by digest. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/pkgs/container/elementary • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205
ATT&CKT1610 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Detection authors validating this rule by deliberately pulling the image into a sandbox
  • Inventory tools (e.g. trivy, syft, grype) running `docker pull` to scan the image (legit but should still be triaged once)
  • GitOps reconciliation re-pulling an already-deployed image after the rule deploys
  • CI build cache warm-up jobs that pre-pull common images
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox", "image-scanner")) and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("trivy.exe", "syft.exe", "grype.exe", "snyk.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host / k8s node that ran the pull and the cluster context; confirm the resolved digest — if it matches `sha256:31ecc5939de6...634255` you have the trojaned image. 2) Contain: cordon and drain the node, kill or `kubectl delete pod` any running containers using the image, patch deployments to `0.23.4` pinned by digest, purge the local image cache (`docker rmi`/`crictl rmi`). 3) Hunt: query the registry mirror / Harbor / ECR pull logs for every previous pull of this image, scan all kustomize/helm/argocd manifests for unpinned references, check workload identity bindings — if the pod ran with cloud IAM roles, those credentials are compromised (see UC #1 runbook).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("docker.exe", "docker", "podman.exe", "podman", "crictl.exe", "crictl", "kubectl.exe", "kubectl", "nerdctl.exe", "nerdctl", "buildah", "skopeo")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary"
| extend IsLatestOrBad = ProcessCommandLine has_any (":latest", ":0.23.3", "sha256:31ecc5939de6") or not(ProcessCommandLine matches regex @":(0\.23\.[4-9]|0\.2[4-9]|[1-9])")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, IsLatestOrBad
| order by Timestamp desc
let TargetImage = "ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary";
union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\docker.exe", "\\podman.exe", "\\crictl.exe", "\\kubectl.exe", "\\nerdctl.exe")
        | where CommandLine has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Source = "SecurityEvent4688"),
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetProcessName has_any ("docker", "podman", "crictl", "kubectl", "nerdctl", "buildah", "skopeo")
        | where TargetProcessCommandLine has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate"),
    (Syslog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "kubelet", "crio")
        | where SyslogMessage has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = "", NewProcessName = ProcessName, CommandLine = SyslogMessage, Source = "Syslog"),
    (AKSAudit
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where Verb in ("create", "update", "patch")
        | where ObjectRef has "pods" or ObjectRef has "deployments" or ObjectRef has "statefulsets" or ObjectRef has "daemonsets" or ObjectRef has "cronjobs"
        | where RequestObject has TargetImage
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = tostring(parse_json(tostring(User)).username), Account = Username, NewProcessName = Verb, CommandLine = tostring(RequestObject), Source = "AKSAudit")
| extend IsLatestOrBad = CommandLine has_any (":latest", ":0.23.3", "sha256:31ecc5939de6") or not(CommandLine matches regex @":(0\.23\.[4-9]|0\.2[4-9]|[1-9])")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Pull of Compromised ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary Container Image
id: 1c5e2a91-7b4d-4f8e-9b2a-8c3d4e5f6a72
description: Detects container runtime / orchestrator pulling the trojaned elementary GHCR image (any tag at or before 0.23.3, especially :latest).
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1610
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\docker.exe'
      - '\podman.exe'
      - '\crictl.exe'
      - '\kubectl.exe'
      - '\nerdctl.exe'
      - '/docker'
      - '/podman'
      - '/crictl'
      - '/kubectl'
      - '/nerdctl'
  selection_img:
    CommandLine|contains: 'ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_img
level: high
(source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) AND (@Image:(*\\docker.exe OR *\\podman.exe OR *\\crictl.exe OR *\\kubectl.exe OR *\\nerdctl.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/docker OR */podman OR */crictl OR */kubectl OR */nerdctl OR */buildah OR */skopeo)) AND (@CommandLine:*ghcr.io\/elementary-data\/elementary* OR @process.command_line:*ghcr.io\/elementary-data\/elementary*)) OR (source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(create OR update OR patch) @requestObject.spec.containers.image:*ghcr.io\/elementary-data\/elementary*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(docker|podman|crictl|kubectl|nerdctl|buildah|skopeo)(\.exe)?$/i CommandLine=/ghcr\.io\/elementary-data\/elementary/i
| ImageTag := regex("ghcr\\.io/elementary-data/elementary(?::(?<tag>[\\w\\.-]+))?", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("docker.exe","docker","podman","podman.exe","crictl","crictl.exe","kubectl","kubectl.exe","nerdctl","nerdctl.exe","buildah","skopeo")) AND Processes.process="*ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary*" AND (Processes.process="*pull*" OR Processes.process="*run*" OR Processes.process="*create*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("docker.exe","docker","podman","podman.exe","crictl","crictl.exe","kubectl","kubectl.exe","nerdctl","nerdctl.exe","buildah","skopeo")) AND Processes.process="*ghcr.io/elementary-data/elementary*" AND (Processes.process="*pull*" OR Processes.process="*run*" OR Processes.process="*create*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Stage-3 exfil archive trin.tar.gz POST via curl --data-binary AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the stage-3 collector packaging harvested credentials into `trin.tar.gz` and exfiltrating via `curl --data-binary` (the exact mechanism named in the article). Fires on either the file write of trin.tar.gz or a curl process command line carrying `--data-binary` together with the C2 host — both are signature-grade for this specific payload. Rationale: Three article-named anchors combined: the archive filename `trin.tar.gz`, the exact `curl --data-binary` invocation, and either the C2 domain or the custom request header `X-Rise-To-The-Trinny: agree`. The triple makes false positives effectively impossible — generic curl POST traffic won't carry these strings. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://github.com/elementary-data/elementary/issues/2205
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1041 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal sandbox / detonation environment running the malware to validate detection (filter by lab host tags)
  • Threat-intel team uploading captured artefacts for analysis where `trin.tar.gz` is the analysed file name
  • Detection-engineering replay of the IOC in a contained VM (should still alert; tag the host as known-test)
  • Forensic copy operations preserving the archive name in evidence storage
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox", "detonation", "malware-lab")) and not (AccountName in~ ("redteam", "sec-research"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm host has the trojaned package or container; capture `trin.tar.gz` if present (it lists exactly which secrets were harvested — irreplaceable for scoping rotation); preserve the curl command line for the exact request body sent. 2) Contain: isolate the host immediately, kill the curl PID, block the C2 host at the proxy and DNS RPZ. 3) Hunt: assume *every* credential reachable from the host is burned — SSH private keys, ~/.git-credentials, gh auth token, AWS keys + IMDSv2 role + Secrets Manager / SSM secrets, GCP ADC, ~/.azure, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.kube/config, /etc/kubernetes/*.conf, ServiceAccount tokens, all .env files to depth 6, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.cargo/credentials.toml, ~/.vault-token, ~/.netrc, ~/.pgpass, ~/.my.cnf, BTC/LTC/DOGE/ZEC/DASH/XMR/XRP wallets, ETH keystores, Cardano/Solana keys. Rotate every one before lifting containment.
let WindowDays = 30d;
let C2 = "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud";
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
        | where FileName in~ ("curl", "curl.exe")
        | where ProcessCommandLine has "--data-binary"
        | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (C2, "trin.tar.gz", "X-Rise-To-The-Trinny")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, Source = "ProcessExec"),
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
        | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
        | where FileName =~ "trin.tar.gz"
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName), Source = "FileWrite")
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowDays = 30d;
let C2 = "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud";
union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/curl"
        | where CommandLine has "--data-binary"
        | where CommandLine has_any (C2, "trin.tar.gz", "X-Rise-To-The-Trinny")
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "SecurityEvent4688"),
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where TargetProcessName has "curl"
        | where TargetProcessCommandLine has "--data-binary"
        | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (C2, "trin.tar.gz", "X-Rise-To-The-Trinny")
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "ImProcessCreate"),
    (ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
        | where TargetFileName =~ "trin.tar.gz"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = ActingProcessName, CommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = "", Source = "ImFileEvent"),
    (Syslog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where SyslogMessage has_any ("trin.tar.gz", "X-Rise-To-The-Trinny", C2)
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = "", NewProcessName = ProcessName, CommandLine = SyslogMessage, ParentProcessName = "", Source = "Syslog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: elementary-data Stealer trin.tar.gz Exfil via curl --data-binary
id: 9f3b1d44-6c2e-4a7f-8d51-3e4f5a6b7c8d
description: Detects the stage-3 collector exfiltrating trin.tar.gz to the elementary-data C2 host via curl --data-binary.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1560.001
  - attack.t1041
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_curl:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '/curl'
    CommandLine|contains: '--data-binary'
  selection_ioc:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud'
      - 'trin.tar.gz'
      - 'X-Rise-To-The-Trinny'
  condition: selection_curl and selection_ioc
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR linux.auditd) AND (@Image:(*\\curl.exe OR *\\CURL.EXE) OR @process.executable.path:(*/curl OR */CURL)) AND (@CommandLine:*--data-binary* OR @process.command_line:*--data-binary*) AND (@CommandLine:(*igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud* OR *trin.tar.gz* OR *X-Rise-To-The-Trinny*) OR @process.command_line:(*igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud* OR *trin.tar.gz* OR *X-Rise-To-The-Trinny*))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/curl(\.exe)?$/i CommandLine=/--data-binary/i CommandLine=/(skyhanni\.cloud|trin\.tar\.gz|X-Rise-To-The-Trinny)/i) OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/trin\.tar\.gz$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
(| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("curl","curl.exe") AND Processes.process="*--data-binary*" AND (Processes.process="*skyhanni.cloud*" OR Processes.process="*trin.tar.gz*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`) | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="trin.tar.gz" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
(| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("curl","curl.exe") AND Processes.process="*--data-binary*" AND (Processes.process="*skyhanni.cloud*" OR Processes.process="*trin.tar.gz*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="trin.tar.gz" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High
Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.
ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Bitwarden CLI Hijacked on npm: Bun-Staged Credential Stealer Targets Developers, GitHub Actions, and AI Tools

StepSecurity
2026-05-04 12 use cases 5 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

@bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 — the official command-line interface for the Bitwarden password manager — was found compromised on npm. A malicious preinstall hook silently bootstraps the Bun JavaScript runtime and launches a 9.7 MB obfuscated credential stealer that targets developer secrets, GitHub Actions environments, and — explicitly — AI coding tool configurations including ~/.claude.json and MCP server configs. All stolen data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and exfiltrated to audit.checkmarx.cx, a domain impersonating the legitimate security company Checkmarx. When GitHub tokens are found, the …
